phasing_details.phase_detail: Whole development - regrading and formalisation of layout

description: Change of use of land from residential garden associated with Willowdene to a Class B8 open-air car storage area, with retention of the existing dwellinghouse in Class C3 use and associated domestic curtilage, together with associated works including permeable hardstanding, installation of palisade fencing and gates, installation of an ancillary office cabin, landscaping and ecological enhancement works, and removal of existing ad hoc structures. (Part-Retrospective application)
decision_conditions: The proposed change of use of former residential garden land to an open-air vehicle storage (Use Class B8), together with associated hardstanding, fencing, gates, office cabin and operational works, would constitute inappropriate development in the Green Belt. The site has not been demonstrated to be Grey Belt land, no evidenced unmet need for the proposed use has been established, and the proposal has not been shown to be in a sustainable or suitable location. The development would harm the openness of the Green Belt and conflict with the purposes of including land within it. No very special circumstances have been demonstrated. The proposal is therefore contrary to paragraphs GB2, GB6 and GB7 of the NPPF, Policy G2 of the London Plan (2021), Policy EM2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), and Policy DMEI 4 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020).

The proposed development, by reason of its extensive hardstanding, regimented vehicle storage layout, office cabin, palisade fencing and commercial appearance, would result in an urbanising and visually intrusive form of development that would harm the character and appearance of the area and the visual amenity of the Green Belt. Insufficient landscaping details have been provided, and no tree survey or arboricultural information has been submitted to demonstrate that retained mature trees would be protected. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policies DMEI 4, DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies G2, D3, D4 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), and paragraphs DP3, GB6 and GB7 of the NPPF.

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that the retained dwelling at Willowdene would provide an acceptable standard of residential amenity. In particular, insufficient information has been submitted regarding the height, design and relationship of the proposed office cabin to the dwelling's rear-facing windows and garden, and the submitted plans fail to clearly show how the residential curtilage would be separated from the commercial storage use. The proposal would therefore harm the outlook and amenity of future occupiers of Willowdene, contrary to Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020).

The applicant has failed to demonstrate that safe and suitable access to the development can be achieved. The submitted information does not demonstrate adequate and permanently available visibility splays or that the largest vehicles likely to serve the development could safely enter and leave the site and negotiate the constrained local highway network, including the narrow bridge. The proposed cycle parking also falls below the applicable minimum standards and therefore fails to fully take up opportunities to encourage sustainable travel. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T1, T5 and T7 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies TR4 and TR6 of the NPPF (2026).

The submitted ecological and Biodiversity Net Gain information fails to provide a robust and accurate assessment of the site's baseline biodiversity value. The BNG Assessment relies on an assumed baseline, does not clearly identify the baseline date, and does not adequately reflect the pre-existing vegetated condition of the site prior to clearance. The applicant has also failed to justify reliance on off-site biodiversity units against the biodiversity gain hierarchy. The proposal therefore fails to demonstrate that the required 10% Biodiversity Net Gain would be secured, contrary to Policy EM7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One (2012), Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies G6 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), the Environment Act 2021 and the NPPF.

The applicant is advised that following refusal of this application, the existing unauthorised use and associated operational development remain unauthorised. The applicant is therefore expected to cease the unauthorised use, reinstate the lawful use of the land, and remove all unauthorised structures, hardstanding, fencing and associated development within a reasonable period. Failure to do so may result in further enforcement action being taken by the Local Planning Authority.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and NPPF (2026).

This is a reminder that Under the terms of the Planning Act 2008 (as amended) and Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), should an application for appeal be allowed, the proposed development would be deemed as 'chargeable development' and therefore liable to pay the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would be calculated in accordance with the London Borough of Hillingdon CIL Charging Schedule 2014 and the Mayor of London's CIL Charging Schedule 2012.
For more information on CIL matters please visit the planning portal page at: www.planningportal.gov.uk/planning/applications/howtoapply/whattosubmit/cil
